# Sculpt.3md native insertion review (read-only, source-proven)

I found no data-loss, atomicity or security defect in insertion. There are three medium issues: two about clarity (where a batch lands, and what a refusal is about) and one about capacity. Everything below comes from reading the source. I did not edit, build, run tests, launch the app or use Bash. I only compared against the base conceptually, without a git diff.

## Actionable defects

**1. Medium (UX): composition insertion silently overwrites tiles, and you can't pick the start cell without painting one.**
- `SculptureSceneInsertion.swift:71-76` writes into consecutive cells and replaces whatever was there.
- The start cell is `selectedCell` (`SculptureCompositionEditor.swift:454`). The only way to set it is `paint()` (`:179-188`), which also paints or erases that cell.
- `load()` resets it to (0,0,0) (`:557`), and the caption only says "Places selected models here." (`:1003`).
- **Repro:** open a new composition (the starter has A at cell 0 and B at cell 2) and insert three files. Cells 0–2 are replaced, so the starter A and B disappear with no warning. Their bindings stay. Undo restores them, and the core test `placingOverAnOccupiedCell…` treats overwriting as intended.
- **Fix:** select a cell without painting it, show the target cells, and either skip occupied cells or confirm before replacing them.

**2. Medium (UX): refusal messages don't name the file or the needed tile size.**
- `SculptureInsertionFiles.swift:22-25` passes decode errors through without the file name. One world file or plain Markdown `.3md` in a 64-file folder refuses the whole batch, and you can't tell which file caused it.
- A child that doesn't fit throws `childDoesNotFit("insert-model-N")`. The editor shows it raw (`SculptureCompositionEditor.swift:478`), skipping the friendlier `validateGraph` message (`:590-616`).
- **Repro:** with the default 24³ tiles, insert a 32-wide model. You see "The rotated model 'insert-model-1' does not fit its reserved tile block." That's a generated ID, and the model isn't rotated.

**3. Medium (capacity): scenes over the portable limit can't take any insertion.**
- Insertion always builds and encodes a portable copy of the parent and result (`SculptureSceneInsertion.swift:67, :105, :138-140`). Shared edits fall back to the native format when portable capacity is exceeded (`SculpturePortableInterchange.swift:92-95`).
- So a scene already showing the "exceeds portable ThreeMD capacity" notice refuses even a 1×1×1 child, though the result would save natively.
- The comment at `:139` says native save uses the same limits, but native saves use the separate composition/world codecs.
- I did not reproduce this at runtime.

**4. Low:** inserted compositions show up as "Map insert-model-N" in the world (`SculptureWorldEditor.swift:111`) and "Nested map" in the composition (`SculptureCompositionEditor.swift:144`). The imported title survives only in the portable snapshot.

**5. Low:** multi-select and folder order is a case-sensitive text sort by path (`SculptureInsertionFiles.swift:13`). `model-10` lands before `model-2`, and your selection order is dropped. The comment at `SculptureSceneInsertion.swift:18` says "selection order", while the spec says "caller input order".

**6. Low:** "Use in a world" stays enabled while insertion is preparing (`SculptureCompositionEditor.swift:1084-1087`). It hands off the pre-insertion composition, and the pending insertion is then likely cancelled when the sheet closes (`:767`). I didn't check how the host dismisses the sheet.

**7. Nit:** each inserted voxel child picks up `sculpt-storage: portable-scene-1` in its own definition (`SculptureThreeMDCodec.swift:44-52`, via `SculptureSceneInsertion.swift:177`). Decoding ignores it, but the saved content differs from a model added any other way.

## Spec consistency
- REQ-RookApp-084 and REQ-RookSculpture-042 exist only in the `.specsync/changes/insert-selected-3md-…/deltas/` files, not in `specs/*/requirements.md`.
- `RookApp.spec.md` lists `SculptureInsertionFiles.swift` but has no insertion behaviour or error cases.
- `RookSculpture.spec.md:259` says `SculptureInsertionError` covers capacity. In fact capacity and fit failures come out as `SculptureCompositionError.tooManyModels`/`childDoesNotFit` and `SculptureWorldError.tooManyInstances`/`invalidOrigin`.
- `RookApp.spec.md:123` says ThreeMD is linked only through RookSculpture, but `SculpturePortableInterchange.swift:5` imports ThreeMD directly. This is probably older than this branch; I couldn't confirm without a diff.
- `docs/file-insertion.md` matches the code on its limits (4,096 entries, 64 files, the 20 MiB total, read-only access, symlink refusal) and on the X spacing. It doesn't mention that occupied cells are overwritten.

## Checked and correct
- **Graphs and IDs:** nested graphs get fresh IDs with no collisions. Unused models are kept and counted toward capacity before anything is copied. Sharing within a file is kept, and inserting the same file twice gives independent copies. ThreeMD scopes plane and reference IDs per definition (`DocumentIdentity.swift:32`), so duplicates across copies are allowed.
- **Metadata:** opaque metadata, preambles, plane attributes and labels, authored plane order and reference order all survive save and reopen. Parent IDs stay exact.
- **Undo and dirty state:** one Undo/Redo restores the whole value plus its portable snapshot in both editors, and dirty state follows the saved baseline.
- **Cancellation and stale results:** cancelling, or a result whose preparation ID has gone stale, never publishes. A changed world revision refuses the result with a message. Any composition edit (`changed()`) cancels the pending insertion.
- **Placement and limits:** world origins use checked Int64 maths plus the anchor bound. Running out of characters, cells, models or instances refuses before any change. Tile fit is checked by `SculptureComposition`.
- **File access:** reads use `O_NOFOLLOW`, non-blocking descriptors, a regular-file check and a byte limit. Access is scoped to each selected file or the folder grant. Folder scanning skips hidden files, packages and symlinks, and its errors are passed on.

## Coverage risks
- No test that a composition edit during preparation drops the result (it relies on `changed()` cancelling).
- No test of the overwrite/selection behaviour from your perspective, or of the capacity-fallback gap.
- No test of a portable save finishing mid-insertion: `retainPortableSnapshot` neither bumps `documentRevision` nor cancels.
- No test of an intermediate directory being swapped for a symlink between folder scan and read.
- No native checks with real panel grants. The "Use in a world" handoff drops portable metadata (probably older behaviour).

No human approval is claimed or implied.

SCULPT_CLAUDE_REVIEW_DONE
[?25h
